rubric_items.reason: Every changed path has a test: the last-visit join, not_seen parsing and filter, yearBefore, the filter applied before paging and in total, the web column and checkbox, and dateOnly.
Most assertions check exact observable results (dates, doctor names, name lists, totals, URLs). The medical-history regex and the first-of-month dateOnly case are weak.
Covers the not_seen=yes 400 field error, the 29 Feb clamp, the leap-year cutoff, local vs UTC midnight both ways, never-visited, a No-show after a visit, and filter-before-paging.
Vitest+Supertest with a throwaway DB and a pinned clock in api/test, Testing Library in web/src/__tests__. Names start with HMS-27 REQ-n and all data is invented. Only test files changed.
No counts or coverage stated. It defers to checks.json and says coverage is skipped, which matches the verifier's coverage step (exit 78, skip).

findings.text: The REQ-12 test's regex only catches allergies, notes and the word 'medical'. A leaked blood group or current-medications field would pass, and the fixture patient has neither, though S-4 AC1 names them.

cites.quote: Given a patient with a blood group, allergies and current medications recorded

findings.suggested_fix: Give the filtered patient a blood group and current medications, then assert that each item's keys exactly match the list-item key set (as PAT-8 does) with not_seen=true.

findings.text: The first-of-month dateOnly case says a zone shift could move the day. A shift only moves it when the runner's zone is behind UTC, and Kolkata and UTC are not, so a shifting implementation would still pass there.

cites.quote: The first of a month stays on that day (a UTC-to-local shift could move it).

findings.suggested_fix: Run the case under a zone behind UTC (for example, stub TZ to America/New_York) so a shifting implementation fails.
